title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-20
lineage: 7inch 2-track Betty Reel w/ dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES @ 44.056 KHz > analog out > dolby A decoder > analog in Fostex D5 @ 48KHz > DATx3 > ZA2 > notch filter > CD-R

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a tight early‑71 Port Chester show, highlighted by a smoking Ripple and Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a clear, crisp soundboard mix with only occasional dropouts, letting the band’s tight arrangements shine. The performance is marked by standout versions of Ripple, Lovelight, Bird Song and the first‑set Cryptical/Other One suite, while the second set falls just short of the first’s intensity. Overall it’s a high‑energy snapshot of a pivotal moment in 1971.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both performance and recording; a few lower scores note minor issues, yielding an overall strong weighted average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Betty Cantor‑sourced soundboard is clear, crisp and lively; occasional dropouts are mentioned but do not detract significantly from overall listenability.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment / The Other One (first‑set suite)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is tight and inventive with strong jams; the second set is solid but not as compelling, ending on a high note with Ripple.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jangly leads throughout, especially an Allman‑like tone on Bird Song and sparkling work on Me & My Uncle; consistently strong guitar presence.
band_member_comments.Phil: Funky, laser‑focused bass lines that drive the band; prominently placed in the mix and highlighted during The Other One intro.
band_member_comments.Bob: Inspired rhythm/lead guitar work on Hard to Handle, Wharf Rat and especially the GDTRFB coda; adds melodic depth.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ fills and his rap on Lovelight add texture; keyboards are bright and complement the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann adapts smoothly after Mickey’s departure, delivering solid drum breaks (notably in The Other One); overall tight but with occasional looseness noted.
